title: Server Rendering and Performance knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Server Rendering and Performance”?
options: Server Rendering and Performance removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Server Rendering and Performance should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Server Rendering and Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Server Rendering and Performance means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
questions.answer_key: Server Rendering and Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Server Rendering and Performance is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” in this lesson?
options: Use “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Choosing CSR, SSR, and SSG” under Server Rendering and Performance. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Server Rendering and Performance”?
options: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
